scenario: A competitive offshore sailing programme selects crew members who demonstrate expert meteorological interpretation OR exceptional boat-handling skill. In the candidate population the two abilities are independent; the OR-gate selection induces a negative collider correlation among selected crew.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (meteorological interpretation) OR (boat-handling skill)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(meteo_skill | ¬boat_handling, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(meteo_skill | boat_handling, selected) and show it equals P(meteo_skill). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between meteorological interpretation and boat-handling skill.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks boat-handling skill must possess meteorological interpretation to be admitted — hence P(meteo_skill|¬boat_handling,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has boat-handling skill is admitted regardless of meteorological interpretation, so P(meteo_skill|boat_handling,sel)=P(meteo_skill)=0.38. The gap (1.0 vs 0.38) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between meteorological interpretation and boat-handling skill observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.38+0.47-0.38×0.47=0.6714. (2) Among candidates without boat-handling skill: only those with meteorological interpretation are selected → P(meteo_skill|¬boat_handling,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with boat-handling skill: selected regardless of meteorological interpretation → P(meteo_skill|boat_handling,sel)=P(meteo_skill)=0.38. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬boat_handling raises P(meteo_skill) from 0.38 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.38,0.47
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6714)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.38)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
